chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his chain, said:

The months for the Hajj are Shawwal, and Dhu al-Qadah, and ten (days) from Dhu al-Hijja; and the months for visitations are twenty (days) from Dhu al-Hijja, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten (days) from the month of Rabi' al-Akhar.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific months and days designated for Hajj and visitations in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi delineates the temporal framework for Hajj and Siyyah, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that distinguishes between the canonical pilgrimage months and the broader period for devotional visits. By specifying these intervals, the hadith provides juristic clarity for distinguishing between the obligatory rites of Hajj and the recommended acts of Ziyarah, which are central to Shia spiritual practice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, by his chain,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The months for the Hajj are Shawwal, and Zil-Qadah, and ten (days) from Zil-Hijja; and the months for visitations are twenty (days) from Zil-Hijjaj, and Al-Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabbi Al-Awwal, and ten (days) from Rabbi Al-Akhar’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali has narrated through the same chain of his narrators has said the following: “He (the Imam) ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the months of al-Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa’dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hajj ah. The visiting months commence from twentieth of Dhu al-Hajj ah onward and includes the month of Muharram, Safar, Rabi’ al-Awwal and ten days of Rabi‘ al-Akhir.’”
